questions.questionMarkup: Efflorescence in saline soils occurs primarily due to
questions.questionText: Efflorescence in saline soils occurs primarily due to

options.html: Downward percolation of water rich in salts into the groundwater table
options.text: Downward percolation of water rich in salts into the groundwater table

options.html: Absorption of carbon dioxide by the soil surface leading to salt precipitation
options.text: Absorption of carbon dioxide by the soil surface leading to salt precipitation

options.html: Upward movement of water from the water table carrying dissolved salts, followed by evaporation at the surface
options.text: Upward movement of water from the water table carrying dissolved salts, followed by evaporation at the surface

options.html: Flow of water from inside the roots into the soil by osmosis
options.text: Flow of water from inside the roots into the soil by osmosis

questions.explanationHtml:
(c)
Downward percolation of water through the soil containing salts is called leaching. The phenomenon
of salts coming up in solution and forming a thin crust on the surface after evaporation of water
is called effloresence.
